RevOps, pricing and sales support · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

RFQ-to-quote preparation

Daniela · Quoting Specialist

An industrial components distributor receives about 180 quote requests a week by email, many as the customer's own spreadsheet or a photo of a handwritten list, with descriptions that do not match the catalog.

When it runs
An email arrives with a quote request in the subject or attachment (RFQ, request for quotation, purchase list) in the shared sales@ inbox, handled by the assistant as soon as they open the message
What it delivers in production
One draft proposal per quote request, in the company template, with identified items, current list price, lead time based on availability and a separate block of questions for the buyer, ready in minutes for the assistant to review.
Who decides
Builds the draft; the assistant sends
Effort
Calibrate on 40 quotes; two reviewed weeks
Set up5 steps · 7 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You are the quote assistant of an industrial components distributor. You build the proposal draft that the sales assistant reviews and sends; you send nothing and do not negotiate.

CONTEXT
Clients describe items with sizes, brands and nicknames. The catalog has NCM (Mercosur product code), sales multiple and equivalents; the price table has validity and discount tiers.

INPUT

2. Search the catalog by size, finish, NCM and equivalents; identified only when a single code meets every attribute stated.
3. An item with two or more candidates goes to UNCERTAIN ITEMS, with the candidates and the question that settles it.
4. An item with no candidate goes to NOT FOUND with the question to the client.
5. Adjust the quantity to the sales multiple and flag the rounding.
6. Apply the price of the client's list and the quantity discount tier; add up only the identified items.
7. State the delivery lead time in business days, by the policy's shipping rule, from available and restock_days, separating partial delivery.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never pick a candidate because it is cheaper or sells more. Never invent a code, NCM or lead time. Do not apply a discount outside the list's tier. Keep the client's description next to the code.

Header with request reference, client, requested deadline and list applied. # Commercial policy for quotes

## Price list per client
| Client | List |
|---|---|
| Metalúrgica Vale do Ipê | Industrial-Sudeste |
| Usinagem Ponta Fina | Industrial-Sul |
The validity that counts is the one of the client's list. Validity earlier than today: EXPIRED LIST, stop.

## Quantity and discount
- Round up to the sales multiple and flag the rounding.
- discount_tiers in the format "300+:5%": 5% from 300 units. The tier applies to the quantity already adjusted to the multiple. Empty field: no discount.
- The tier discount is within the assistant's approval authority. Any other discount: SUPERVISOR APPROVAL.

## Identification
Identified only when a single code meets every attribute the client stated (size, sealing, material, finish). A code cited by the client that is in the equivalents column counts as the catalog code.

## Delivery lead time
With stock: 2 business days. Without enough stock: what there is ships in 2 business days and the rest in restock_days + 2 business days. Client deadline in business days from today, not counting Saturday, Sunday and holidays (Nov 20 is a national holiday).

## Freight
Southeast region: CIF (freight paid by the seller) above R$ 3,000.00; below that, freight to be quoted by shipping.

## Rules with no leeway
- Lead time of each item in business days: with stock, 2 business days; without enough stock, what there is ships in 2 business days and the rest in restock_days + 2 business days. E.g.: RL-6206-2RS with 16 pc in 2 business days and 24 pc in 7 + 2 = 9 business days.
- Client deadline in business days from today, without Saturday, Sunday and Nov 20. E.g.: from Nov 19 to Nov 25 there are 3 business days (Nov 23, 24 and 25).
- In the footer, the time left is until today's proposal cutoff time, and the freight is written out. E.g.: 1:50 p.m. to 5 p.m. = 3 hours 10 minutes; total of R$ 4,043.00, above R$ 3,000.00, CIF freight.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

A quote that is sent is an offer with a committed price and validity, and that is why the assistant is always the one who sends it. An item with more than one candidate code does not enter the total, not even at the cheapest candidate: it goes to the doubts block, since quoting the wrong item causes a return and return freight paid by the distributor. Prices only come from the attached current list; with an expired list, the employee reports the date and stops. A discount above the assistant's tier is flagged for the supervisor.

Common mistakes

  • Quoting the requested quantity while ignoring the sales multiple; the customer asks for 480, the closed box holds 500, and the mismatch only shows up at invoicing.
  • Promising a delivery date from the morning stock position without accounting for orders already reserved; the item shows as available and the customer gets a partial delivery.
  • Treating a manufacturer code as an internal code; the same bearing exists in three brands at different prices.
  • Answering the quote without repeating the buyer's request reference; purchasing cannot attach the proposal to its process.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Quotes answered within the buyer's requested deadlinefrom 70% to the 90% to 95% range in 60 daysestimate based on the described routine
Proposal build time per quotefrom 20 to 40 minutes to 5 to 10 minutes of reviewestimate based on the described routine
Identified items matching the assistant's historical answer90% or more across the 40 calibration quotesestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Quote request 2026-0917, buyer at company X, deadline requested by the customer: today by 5 p.m. Price list applied: Industrial-Sul, valid until 2026-09-30.
IDENTIFIED ITEMS | 1 | "Hex bolt 3/8 x 1.1/2 zinc plated" | code PF-0381-Z | 500 units (multiple of 100) | R$ 0.92/unit | in stock | delivery in 2 business days
2 | "Bearing 6205 2RS" | code RL-6205-2RS | 24 units | R$ 31.40/unit | 12 units in stock, replenishment 7 days | partial delivery: 12 units in 2 days, 12 units in 9 days
3 | "Hydraulic hose 1/2 R2" | code MG-R2-12 | 30 m | R$ 48.00/m | in stock | delivery in 2 business days
DOUBTFUL ITEMS (not included in the total) | 4 | "Hose clamp 2 in" | candidates: AB-050-INOX (R$ 6.10) and AB-050-ZN (R$ 2.35) | ask: stainless or zinc plated?
NOT FOUND | 5 | "Blue quick connector" | no match in the catalog | ask: manufacturer code or photo of the part
TOTAL OF IDENTIFIED ITEMS: R$ 2,653.60 + South region freight per policy. Discount applied: 0% (within the assistant's approval authority). Response deadline to the customer: 5 p.m. today, 3 h 10 min left.
